::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
The facility this tracker's own About page flagged as its highest-priority missing entry: SMIC's primary advanced-node fab in Zhangjiang — the JV (established 1 December 2016, SMIC holding 41.56% after the December 2025 capital increase took registered capital from $6.5B to $10.077B) that operates SN1, the only confirmed 7nm-class (N+2/N+3) production line in China and the fab behind the Kirin 9000S/9030 story. Unlike the 28nm-era JVs in this tracker, its exposure is not mature-node competition with the West but the export-control frontier itself: EUV is banned, and it produces leading-edge-adjacent logic on DUV multi-patterning.
:::

**Chinese name:** 中芯南方集成电路制造有限公司 (Zhōngxīn Nánfāng Jíchéng Diànlù Zhìzào Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

12-inch FinFET wafers at 14nm and below for Huawei (Kirin SoCs) and, per unverified self-media claims only, other domestic advanced customers; SN2 doubles as an equipment/tool-verification line for domestic toolmakers.

## Why does it matter?

Capacity figures here are the most contested numbers in the tracker: official filings give registered capital but not output, and media claims of ~35k wafers/month N+2 rising to ~70k in 2026 (and Huawei taking a fixed share) come from self-media sources and are explicitly NOT verified by this tracker. What is confirmed by primary/research sources: the December 2025 capital increase with Big Fund III taking an 8.361% stake, and TechInsights' confirmation of N+3 production in the Kirin 9030 (December 2025).

## Technology Node Trajectory

- **2020**: 14nm FinFET (SN1)
- **2023**: N+2 — Kirin 9000S class (TechInsights teardown)
- **2025**: N+3 — Kirin 9030 class (TechInsights, Dec 2025)

## Project Timeline

- **Dec 2016** — SMIC South (中芯南方) established as SMIC–Big Fund–Shanghai fund JV in Zhangjiang
- **Sep 2019** — First FinFET lithography tool installed; SN1 targeted at 35,000 wafers/month
- **Dec 2025** — Capital increase completed: registered capital $6.5B → $10.077B; Big Fund III appears as 8.361% shareholder; SMIC retains control at 41.56%
